title: A new analytical finding for the Born-Infeld integral potential
authors: Leonardo Paulo Guimarães De Assis, Priscila Valdênia dos Santos, Sergio de Oliveira Vellozo, José Abdala Helayël Neto
abstract: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.
summary: This work develops an analytical approximation for the Born-Infeld potential, interpreting it as a combination of Coulomb and Yukawa terms representing vacuum polarization. By applying this potential as a perturbation to the hydrogen atom, the authors calculate energy shifts and derive model-dependent lower bounds on the fundamental BI field parameter $b$ by comparing results to experimental atomic spectra.
main_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty of using the Born-Infeld (BI) integral potential in closed form for physical calculations, specifically deriving experimental constraints on the fundamental BI parameter $b$.
main_result: The BI potential can be analytically approximated as a difference between a Coulomb-type and a Yukawa-type potential, leading to calculable, model-dependent lower bounds on the maximum field intensity parameter $b$ by comparing predicted atomic energy shifts with high-precision spectroscopy.
method: The authors use analytical approximations of the BI potential, treat the effect as a perturbation to the hydrogen atom Hamiltonian, and compare the resulting energy shifts with established spectroscopic data.
model_or_system: The system is the hydrogen atom governed by the Born-Infeld Electrodynamics (BIE) potential, which is a nonlinear extension of Maxwell's equations designed to regularize the self-energy of a point charge.
key_observables: First-order energy shifts ($\delta E$) in hydrogen-like atoms for $s$- and $p$-states, and the maximum field intensity parameter $b$.
important_parameters: The BI characteristic length scale ($r_b$), the fundamental field parameter ($b$), and the Bohr radius ($a$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve using the small-distance expansion of the BI potential ($r \ll r_b$) and treating the BI effect as a first-order perturbation using the unperturbed Coulomb wave functions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the exact BI potential numerically against the derived Coulomb-plus-Yukawa approximation. Figure 2 shows the radial distribution of the polarized charge. Table 2 compares calculated energy shifts for $2p 	o 1s$ transitions against experimental data.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the analytical approximation of the BI potential. It then applies this potential perturbatively to the hydrogen atom Hamiltonian to calculate energy shifts. Finally, it compares these calculated shifts against high-precision spectroscopic data to constrain the parameter $b$.
why_interesting: While the core physics is QED/Electrodynamics, the methodology of using high-precision spectroscopic measurements to constrain fundamental parameters of modified field theories (like BI theory) is relevant to AMO physics, particularly in precision measurements involving atomic structure.
